historical_references.reference: King Kaustavakarna, a powerful king mentioned in the ancient Indian epic 'Mahabharata', is known for his strategic skills and immense knowledge. He was a descendant of the Yadava dynasty and ruled the kingdom of Haihayas. He was so named because of his 'kaustav' (knowledge) which helped him make wise decisions and lead his kingdom effectively.

Another reference to Kaustav is that of a Jain sage, also named Kaustubh or Kaustav, who is considered a Tirthankar or a Jina in Jainism. He lived during the 12th century BCE and is known for his deep spiritual insight and enlightenment. He attained kevaljnan (omniscience) and became a teacher of Jain dharma.
